Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
After three days of meetings between President Trump and China's president, one of the few
concrete outcomes is a reduction of tariff rates on a small fraction of goods the two
countries trade with each other.
And Pierre's Emily Fang has more.
After Trump visited Beijing in May, the two countries have been working to find 30 billion
dollars of non-sensitive goods each to reduce tariffs on.
But that's a small slice of the more than $400 billion volume of US-China annual trade.
And two ongoing trade investigations into China on potentially unfair trading practices
will likely raise overall US tariff rates on China again in the coming weeks.
Following Xi's visit to the US, the two countries have also agreed to start an AI dialogue starting
in November.
The US and China held high-level AI dialogues during the Biden administration, where both
Biden and Xi Jinping agreed AI should remain under human control.
Xi repeated the need for humans to control AI in his opening remarks while visiting Washington

Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
CNN is getting a new owner.
Paramount is taking over CNN parent Warner Brothers Discovery, and David Ellison controls
Paramount.
Ellison's family is also a supporter of President Trump.
Media observers are now looking at what that will mean for CNN's news coverage.
NPR's David Folkenflick has more.
They're probably going to see appointed within CNN somebody who's willing to do business

what kind of coverage the Ellison's might be interested in.
You know, you saw at two major publications taken over by Rupert Murdoch, the media magnate

There were such boards created.
And after sort of raising a question here and there, he just kind of ignored and then overrode

Here's NPR's David Folkenflick with our report.
A nor'easter is continuing to bring powerful winds, local floods and canceled events from
the mid-Atlantic to New England, NPR's Ava Berger reports.
In Atlantic City, New Jersey, Talia Manno saw a car totaled from flooding on her street.
She said she hadn't seen so much water since Hurricane Sandy.
The water was just like you could literally see waves on my steps.
You could see waves on the steps.
That's how much water was there.
Jessica Lizboa was out on an Atlantic Ocean cruise as the storm grew.
It felt honestly like a rollercoaster.

downpour.
So we met in a day like this and we're also getting married on a day like this.
Local flooding, heavy rain, and high winds are expected to continue to pummel the East

Several states have made emergency declarations.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
And this is NPR News.
President Trump Saturday rejected a proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran said it would agree to the opening and resume talks on its nuclear program in seven
days if the U.S. ended its naval blockade of the country, waved sanctions on Iranian
oil sales, and began a ceasefire that included Lebanon.
Trump said Iran wanted a deal because it's losing so badly.
Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok are all refusing to run advertisements for
an upcoming documentary on billionaire Elon Musk and Piers Bobby Allen reports.
The documentary is called Musk.
It's by Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney, and it's set for release next month.
The film is a scathing look at the tech mogul's life from his childhood in South Africa, his
rise in Silicon Valley, including his takeover of the site formerly known as Twitter, along
with his time in the White House.
Gibney asks, "How did one man become so powerful?"
It's a message deemed too political by meta, YouTube, and TikTok, all of which have refused
to carry ads about the film.
That's according to a person close to the production who wasn't authorized to speak
publicly.
Earlier this month, lawyers for Musk threatened to file a defamation lawsuit over the film.
Musk would not sit for an interview with Gibney.
Instead, he used an AI-generated avatar of Musk as a stand-in.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
In college football, top-ranked Texas needed a full four quarters to hold off #14 Tennessee
Saturday, 20-17, in Ann Arbor, Iowa, drove 91 yards and scored a touchdown as time ran

Jeremiah Smith tied an Ohio State record with four touchdown catches as the Buckeyes beat
